issue_context.title: Modbus: writeCoil() operation not supported on slave
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
A user reported that the Modbus switch can properly read the state, but it's not able to write the new state to the Modbus slave.
After further investigation, it seems that the slave doesn't support the `writeCoil()` operation. However, it supports an equivalent `writeCoils()` operation with `count=1`.

Our Modbus implementation of the coil switch doesn't count with such a corner case. However, there may be more devices like this. We should probably add a new configuration parameter to force use of the `writeCoils()` method instead of the `writeCoil()`. Alternatively, we could have this as a fallback if we detect an exception, but I think this will slow-down the update process.

To debug the issue, I worked directly with the `pymodbus` REPL. We use `pymodbus` as the underlying library in our integration. I don't have exact Home Assistant config.

Here`s an output from the REPL:
```python
> client.write_coil address=145 unit=7 value=1                                                                                                                                      
{
    "original_function_code": "5 (0x5)",
    "error_function_code": "133 (0x85)",
    "exception code": 1,
    "message": "IllegalFunction"
}

> client.write_coils address=145 unit=7 count=1 values=1                                                                                                                            
{
    "address": 145,
    "count": 1
}

> client.write_coils address=145 unit=7 count=1 values=0                                                                                                                            
{
    "original_function_code": "15 (0xf)",
    "error_function_code": "143 (0x8f)",
    "exception code": 3,
    "message": "IllegalValue"
}

> client.write_coils address=145 unit=7 count=1 values=0,0                                                                                                                          
{
    "address": 145,
    "count": 2
}

```

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: N/A
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): N/A
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): native / Pyhon3 virtualenv / macOS Big Sur
- Integration causing this issue: Modbus
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/switch.modbus/
comments:
Hey there @adamchengtkc, @janiversen, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`modbus`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L281) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

That looks like a real problem to me, I think adding a new config parameter might be the better way. And since I have a proposal for the new configuration ready (just waiting for my outstanding PR to be merged) I can add it there.

I checked pymodbus 2.5 it seems to have the same problem.
stupid question could we not simple just use writeCoils() always ? just a thought.

> "could we not simple just use writeCoils() always"

Perhaps we could, but by doing this we might potentially break compatibility with other devices. You know well that the Modbus implementation on devices is by far not perfect. What if there's a device, which accepts only the `writeCoil()` operation?

I think the best way to handle this issue is to add a new parameter. Feel free to add it to your proposal. In the mean time, I will try to get more information.
Just thinking: besides Modbus Switch, the Light and Cover are affected as well. We should also check the Climate.

I have just started a branch to handle your issue as well as a couple of other issues.

I am thinking of adding a new configuration item:
read_multiple_count
which will use read_coils/read_registers and if count is greater than one, add e.g. new sensors (mysensor (configured) and then mysensor_2 etc.) automatically.
I think that will really limit the use of structure.

what do you think ?

I think it's still better to define sensors explicitly. Also, your suggestion would work only for coils, not for registers. Perhaps we should approach this the easiest way - by introducing a parameter. It is a very specific corner case. Therefore, it should be supported, but I wouldn't complicate other things because of it.

I did not like to add a parameter for such a corner case, however your problem is real.

It is interesting that for registers we have been able to do write_register/write_registers for quite a while, with my PR it is now legal to do write_coil/write_coils.

As you say this is a corner case, so the user need to do something, he/she cannot use turn_on/turn_off but need to do a service call. I think that is fair trade off for such a corner case.

review_comments: The state is validated as a boolean in the service schema. How would it be a list?

ups...I isolated this PR from a bigger PR (in preparation) that add testing of write calls, but I forgot this one, sorry about that.

Thanks for catching it.
